quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Does not increase crash risk.
Helps you react faster to dangers.
Often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to dangerous decisions.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a common cause of crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. This will blind you. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign alerts you that bicycles may be crossing the road.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming vehicles.
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
In a curve with no oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lot entrances, or alleyways. Do not pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and road markings permit it, and only when you have enough space to do so safely.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may pull out without seeing you.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses grip on wet road surfaces, you should:

options.text: Keep a steady speed to get better grip.
Brake hard to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slowly reduce speed and do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce speed and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: At speeds as low as 30 mph in heavy rain, your tires may ride on water instead of gripping the road. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slowly reduce your speed and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?

options.text: Breathe fresh air.
Let your body process it over time.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let your body process it over time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol works quickly but leaves your system slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not reduce blood alcohol. Time is the only way to lower it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
Pump the brakes quickly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of traffic.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if a tire blows. Hold the steering wheel tight and remove your foot from the accelerator to let the vehicle slow down. Brake lightly when safe. Move to the shoulder only after the car has slowed significantly.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and try to pass you in unsafe ways.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in the fog.
Staring at the road ahead of your vehicle.
Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare only at the road ahead. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beams.

questions.question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate. After the gate is raised, wait until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming before crossing.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights?

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, and proceed once the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warning signs, lights, or flaggers tell you a train is coming. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signs. Always signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: If you drive slower than traffic flow, you will most likely:

options.text: Block traffic and receive a ticket.
Improve traffic flow.
Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block traffic and receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slower in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block traffic movement, you may get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic unless traffic exceeds the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Watch for people crossing your path.
No passing zone.
Work zone ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This orange warning sign alerts drivers that roadwork is coming. Stay alert for temporary traffic control devices in work zones.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity relate to vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and crash severity. Faster vehicles cause worse collisions and serious injuries. Increase your following distance as you drive faster so you can stop safely.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events:

options.text: Causes traffic to back up.
Prevents rear-end crashes.
Helps traffic flow by preventing crashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes traffic to back up.
questions.explanation: Avoid slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events. This is called "rubbernecking" and causes traffic to back up.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers only.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, stand, or park at a red-painted curb.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther back from the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When it is hard to see because of darkness or bad weather, stay farther back from other cars. This gives you more time to react to dangers you cannot see.
